predecessors.name: Kalhora dynasty
predecessors.text: Sindh, which the Talpurs took from the Kalhoras at the Battle of Halani in 1783

successors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
successors.text: Sindh without the Khairpur branch, annexed to the Bombay Presidency of British India under the East India Company after the battles of Miani (17 February 1843) and Hyderabad/Dubba (24 March 1843)

successors.name: Khairpur State
successors.text: the northern Khairpur branch, which 'continued in upper Sindh as the Khairpur princely state' (Talpur infobox); 15,730 km2 on the Khairpur page, drawn here as a 70 km disc round Khairpur (15,427 km2)

ledger.x: 1783: Mir Fateh Ali Khan Talpur defeats the Kalhoras at Halani and declares himself Rais of Sindh.

wars.name: Shah Shuja's invasion of Sindh
wars.outcome: The Talpur brothers united and defeated him.

wars.name: British capture of Karachi
wars.outcome: The British held Karachi from 1839 and pressed on Hyderabad, forcing tribute.

wars.name: British conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: British victory at Miani (17 February 1843) and Hyderabad/Dubba (24 March 1843); Sindh annexed to the Bombay Presidency; Khairpur, whose Amir Napier had won over, survived as a princely state.
